liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): One of the better later era performances, featuring a MIDI mind meltdown; Listed as a highlight, alongside Althea, Ramble on Rose, and China Cat [23][27][29]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): By this song, the band is in the groove and rolling [25]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): The song builds until Bobby yells his guts out [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-09-20.schoeps.wiley.11633.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 179 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Digital pops and dropouts in Truckin' were removed using Cool Edit Pro [1]
- **gd1990-09-20.schoepsmk4.bratman.9989.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Secondary source supplies patches in Truckin' at 6:30 and 8:40 [3]
- **gd1990-09-20.150669.nak300.boedicker.flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 168 min [5]
- **gd90-09-20.sbd.ashley.14855.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 180 min; rated 4.77/5 by 48 [6]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is rated A+++, though it has an overabundance of synthetic thunder; Music and vocals are bright and clear, with a powerful audience present [24][31]

## Around the show

- New members Vince and Bruce put significant effort into their performances [25]
- Listener stood by rangers' boards, fifth show of a six-night run [26]
- Listener heard the band seemingly starting to play St. Stephen after Dark Star [27]
- The crowd shook Madison Square Garden, nearly tearing the building down during Dark Star [28]
- Phil edged Jerry to start with Althea, but Bob won with Stranger [32]
- Bruce pounded the piano harder as the band built on the Garden floor [33]
- Thanks given to Barry, the security guy, for assistance [4]
- Bruce's unfamiliarity makes the show less perfunctory than most late era performances [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-09-20.schoeps.wiley.11633.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Dave Brotman; transferred by Tim Wiley; source: FOB-AUD(Scheops)>DAT>CDR> [1]
- **gd1990-09-20.schoepsmk4.bratman.9989.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Darrin Sacks; source: Recorded by Dave Bratman FOB DFC, (Section 2, row 15, seat 1) Schoeps MK4/CMC3 (ortf/110deg)>Oade PS>Oade Mod. SV255 (MIT reference XLR interconnects). [3]. Also: Secondary source is a Healy SBD/AUD Ultramix transferred to DAT then CD-R [3]
- **gd1990-09-20.150669.nak300.boedicker.flac1644**: taped by Taped By Dave Boedicker,Official Taper Section.; transferred by Dave Boedicker; source: Nakamichi 300 Mics W/CP4 Shotguns>Sony WM-D6C Cassette Deck>1 TDM MA-90 Metal Cassette Tape(1stSet) And 1 100 Minute [5]. Also: Tape flips after Ramble On Rose and Throwing Stones clipped initial seconds of next songs [5]
- **gd90-09-20.sbd.ashley.14855.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead Madison Square Garden](https://wallpaperhdcornelia.blogspot.com/2021/05/grateful-dead-madison-square-garden.html) [38]

By this song, the band is in the groove and rolling
Listener stood by rangers' boards, fifth show of a six-night run
Listener heard the band seemingly starting to play St. Stephen after Dark Star
Listed as a highlight, alongside Althea, Ramble on Rose, and China Cat
The crowd shook Madison Square Garden, nearly tearing the building down during Dark Star
A well-jammed six-minute pre-verse performance, getting way out there on the back end
Music and vocals are bright and clear, with a powerful audience present
Phil edged Jerry to start with Althea, but Bob won with Stranger
Bruce pounded the piano harder as the band built on the Garden floor
Digital pops and dropouts in Truckin' were removed using Cool Edit Pro
Secondary source is a Healy SBD/AUD Ultramix transferred to DAT then CD-R
Secondary source supplies patches in Truckin' at 6:30 and 8:40
Thanks given to Barry, the security guy, for assistance
Tape flips after Ramble On Rose and Throwing Stones clipped initial seconds of next songs
